title: epan: Fix relative time if the first frame with a TS isn't frame 1
description:
Get rid of the odd hack where frame_data->frame_ref_num is 0 if
this is a reference frame and just set frame_data->frame_ref_num
to the frame number used for relative timestamp comparisons in
every case, even if it's frame_data->num. That simplifies the
logic, and frame_data already has the ref_time bitfield for telling
if this is a time reference frame.

Note that there's a slight distinction between "this is a time
reference frame" and "this is the frame used for relative time
stamp comparisons." The first frame in a capture with a timestamp
is the latter but not the former (unless specifically marked as
such by the user.) That can also happen in the odd situation where
the user has marked a frame without a timestamp as a "reference
time frame" (the next frame with a timestamp becomes the frame
used for time comparisons but is not technically a reference time
frame itself.)

See the file in #19896 for an example. Ping #20691.


(cherry picked from commit 98a62adece5345e113aeb679ca37924b93fa0835)

Co-authored-by: John Thacker <johnthacker@gmail.com>

changes_data.diff:
@@ -73,6 +73,7 @@ typedef struct _frame_data {
   GHashTable  *dependent_frames;     /**< A hash table of frames which this one depends on */
   const struct _color_filter *color_filter;  /**< Per-packet matching color_filter_t object */
   uint32_t     cum_bytes;    /**< Cumulative bytes into the capture */
+  /* XXX - cum_bytes presumably ought to be 64-bit as well now */
   uint8_t      tcp_snd_manual_analysis;   /**< TCP SEQ Analysis Overriding, 0 = none, 1 = OOO, 2 = RET , 3 = Fast RET, 4 = Spurious RET  */
   /* Keep the bitfields below to 24 bits, so this plus the previous field
      are 32 bits. (XXX - The previous field could be a bitfield too.) */
@@ -90,7 +91,10 @@ typedef struct _frame_data {
   unsigned int tsprec           : 4; /**< Time stamp precision -2^tsprec gives up to femtoseconds */
   nstime_t     abs_ts;       /**< Absolute timestamp */
   nstime_t     shift_offset; /**< How much the abs_tm of the frame is shifted */
-  uint32_t     frame_ref_num; /**< Previous reference frame (0 if this is one) */
+  uint32_t     frame_ref_num; /**< Reference frame for relative timestamps (can be this frame) */
+  /* frame_ref_num == num if ref_time == true, but also if this is the first
+   * record that has_ts (or if somehow a record without a TS is a reference
+   * time frame, the first frame after that with has_ts == true.) */
   uint32_t     prev_dis_num; /**< Previous displayed frame (0 if first one) */
 } frame_data;
